summary: Per-category free-list allocator for a custom heap. Aligns the request up to an 8-byte boundary, walks the per-category free list (head at this+0x4 + 4*cat + 48) for a first-fit block, and when none fits allocates a fresh block through MallocWrapper (chunk budget from dword_5AF8B8/dword_5AF8C0, halving on OOM, erroring through ShortComputation_5f0e). New blocks are chained into the list and the running total at this+0x4C is incremented. The found block is then carved: its free size shrinks by the request and a pointer 16 bytes past the block header (which carries size fields at +8 and +4) is returned.

local_names.a1: allocator object (vtable at +0, free-list base pointer at +4, byte counter at +0x4C)
local_names.v11: this+4, base pointer of the per-category free-list head array
local_names.v12: address of the free-list head for category a2
local_names.v13: previous block while walking the list (null when no block fits)
local_names.v5: chosen block, or freshly allocated block

operations.description: Reject oversized requests: when a3 exceeds 0x3B9AC9F0, call ShortComputation_5f0e(a1, 1) as the error handler for an oversized allocation
Align the request up to the next 8-byte boundary: v3 = a3 + (8 - (a3 & 7)) when a3 is not already a multiple of 8

Category initialization for a2 >= 2: write constant 12 to the sub-object at obj+0x14 and the category index to obj+0x18, where obj is the object whose pointer lives at this+0x0 (the vtable pointer used by the virtual dispatch)
Invoke the category-initialization callback through the vtable stored at *a1 (obj+0x0), passing the allocator itself
Compute the free-list head for category a2 as this+4 + 4*a2 + 48 (v11 = this+0x4 is the head-array base)

Walk the category free list tracking the previous block v13, stopping at the first block whose size field (v5+8) is at least the aligned request v3; when the list is exhausted (v5 null) a new block must be allocated
Budget a new block: total v6 = request + 16 for the block header, with the chunk size taken from dword_5AF8C0[a2] when a list block exists or dword_5AF8B8[a2] otherwise, capped at 1000000000 - v6
Allocate the new block with MallocWrapper(a1, v7 + v6), retrying with v7 halved on failure and invoking ShortComputation_5f0e(a1, 2) once v7 drops below 0x32 (out-of-memory)

Account and link the new block: add v7 + v6 to the running byte counter at this+0x4C (v11+72), zero the block's forward/backward links, set its size to v3 + v7, and insert it at the head of the category list
Carve the request out of the found block: reduce the block size field (v5+8) by v3 and advance the data offset field (v5+4) by v3
Return the payload pointer: block base + prior data offset + 16 (skipping the block header). Consumed by MemoryAllocatorWithChunking, ChunkedBufferAlloc, LinkedListNodeAllocAndInsert and sub_51623E

clean_pseudocode: align request v3 up to 8 bytes;
while (block && block->size < v3) { prev = block; block = block->next; }
do { block = MallocWrapper(a1, chunk + v3 + 16); chunk >>= 1; }
init block links, size = v3 + chunk; link into list;
